Root Cause: CHW pump failure or strainer clog.
Chain Effect: Flow through the evaporator drops. The refrigerant over-cools the stagnant water, risking a freeze-up trip.

Root Cause: Air/moisture leaked into the low side.
Chain Effect: Air creates a blanket in the condenser that refrigerant cannot penetrate. This causes high head pressure similar to fouling, but persists after cleaning.

Root Cause: Oil migration from sump to tubes.
Chain Effect: Oil coats the evaporator tubes, creating a thermal barrier. The machine loses cooling capacity even though the refrigerant charge is correct.

The gate is wide open. Liquid refrigerant floods the evaporator and enters the compressor suction, risking catastrophic slugging as liquid hits the spinning blades.
The throttle is stuck at idle. The building gets hot because the chiller cannot ramp up, and the low flow puts the machine at risk of surging.

Root Cause: Tower fan motor or belt failure.
Chain Effect: Water returning from the tower gets hotter. This forces condenser pressure up until the compressor can no longer climb the pressure hill.

Root Cause: Oil pump failure or plugged filter.
Chain Effect: The oil pump loses its pressure fight against the refrigerant. Without a differential pressure of 18–25 psid, the bearings lose their oil film and the machine trips to prevent damage.

Root Cause: High Lift vs. Low Flow imbalance.
Chain Effect: Refrigerant gas loses momentum and falls backward through the impeller. This creates violent vibration shocks and power pulses until the machine trips.
